transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-05 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya, Arjun, Liam (Redwood) / Nora, Samir, Priya, Diego (Lattice)

Summary (auto): discussion about renewal timing, capacity bump, and whether Lattice will take an EU on-prem deployment for regulated customers. Pilot and security artifacts requested.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, quick roll call?
[00:06] Nora (Lattice): Nora here, hi Maya, Samir and Priya and Diego on as well.
[00:09] Samir: yep Samir, infra.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, legal.
[00:13] Maya: great. quick agenda: capacity numbers, on-prem option in EU, compliance pack, and next-steps. Arjun will cover the pilot details.
[00:22] Arjun (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll be brief — we looked at your usage traces, your 95th token latency is around 420ms on current hosted plan, with bursty spikes during morning traffic. if we move to reserved capacity with smarter batching we can get that down to ~200-250ms at steady state.
[00:38] Diego (Lattice): 420ms — that aligns with what Diego saw in prod. our enterprise customers in germany expect sub-300 for chat.
[00:45] Nora: correct, EU customers are the stickiest but also most sensitive to both latency and data locality. hence the ask about EU on-prem variant.
[00:54] Maya: totally, and that ties back to the renewal. we can do either dedicated reserved capacity in eu-west region, or a private on-prem package where you host inference inside your VPC or co-lo. both have different pricing and operational support.
[01:10] Samir: can you give a rough delta in unit cost between hosted dedicated and on-prem? like percent change?
[01:16] Maya: rough ballpark — dedicated reserved (Redwood Dedicated) is about 25-35% more predictable but still lower ops on your side. On-prem has higher setup and one-time costs but gives you full egress control and may lower per-token costs at scale — rough net could be similar over 12-24 months depending on utilization. i'll put numbers in the quote.
[01:35] Priya: from legal — if we go on-prem, we need to understand where the control plane lives, audit logs, and who retains keys. KMS question is big for us.
[01:44] Liam (Redwood CSM): good point. for Redwood Private on-prem we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM, and the control plane can live in your VPC with optional hardened connectivity back to our management plane. we'll include the data flow diagram in the pack.
[01:59] Nora: are there any differences in failover and fallback if we choose on-prem vs dedicated? we want graceful degradation to a hosted endpoint if an on-prem node fails.
[02:08] Arjun: yes, that's supported — smart routing can failover to a compatible model in the Redwood-hosted infra. there are policy knobs: latency-first vs cost-first. downside is that fallbacks may increase egress/latency for some calls.
[02:24] Diego: okay that's acceptable as long as routing is deterministic and we can test it.
[02:29] Samir: about the pilot — what's the scope? we need concrete tests for throughput and seq lengths.
[02:34] Arjun: pilot plan — 2-4 hour runs across peak patterns: short chat sessions and long generation. we'll measure per-token throughput, end-to-end latency, tail latencies, and memory/KV cache behavior. will also run failsafe cutover to hosted endpoint to validate fallbacks.
[02:53] Nora: fine. timeline wise we'd want pilot before we sign the renewal.
[02:57] Maya: agreed. target pilot week — 6/14 — gives us time to provision nodes and prep test harness.
[03:05] Priya: on contracts — legal wants explicit SLAs and a clear statement of work for on-prem install, rollback, support tiers, and indemnity language for data processing.
[03:16] Maya: yep we can include optional SLA tiers in the SOW. we'll give a standard 99.9% and a premium 99.95 for dedicated plans; on-prem SLA will depend on customer-managed infra but we can commit to our control-plane uptime and support response times.
[03:33] Samir: one technical Q — does Redwood's runtime support quantized models on-prem? we use int8 in some paths.
[03:39] Arjun: yes, runtime supports quantized kernels and we can ship model variants (fp16, int8) — note performance varies. also, some words in our perf notes — kv cache eviction patterns can affect long-context convo perf, we'll include specific tuning for your long sessions.
[03:58] Diego: slight transcription note (laughs) — it said K-V cash in an earlier doc, but you know what we mean.
[04:03] (laughter)
[04:06] Nora: any blockers from Redwood side?
[04:08] Liam: nothing blocking; just need confirmation on desired commit term (12 vs 24 months), and whether you'd like us to include hardware procurement assist for on-prem.
[04:18] Nora: budget team prefers 12 months with an option to extend; but if the price delta is compelling we'll consider 24.
[04:24] Priya: legal will push for some flexibility on termination during the first 90 days of on-prem due to installation risks.
[04:31] Maya: understood — we'll propose phased billing: a set-up milestone, then monthly usage/commit invoices.
[04:37] Arjun: for the pilot, we'll want a small temporary quota in EU on-prem staging and a hosted fallback to simulate cross-region routing. Diego, can your team stand up a lab cluster?
[04:49] Diego: yes we can, will need spec from Arjun.
[04:52] Arjun: i'll send a minimal spec — 4x A10G-ish nodes with 256GB ram, nvlink optional, and 10g network recommended. that's for a meaningful pilot to stress kv cache and batching.
[05:10] Samir: that spec is fine; we'll validate with our infra team.
[05:14] Maya: ok quick recap / next steps: i'll send the revised quote with 12/24 options and the on-prem cost breakdown, Arjun will send the pilot plan/spec, Liam will share SOC2 + KMS docs, you (Nora/Samir) will confirm SLO targets and infra spec, and Priya will route SOW redlines to us.
[05:33] Nora: sounds good. can we lock a follow-up in two weeks to review pilot results and the draft SOW?
[05:38] Maya: yes, let's tentatively schedule 6/23.
[05:41] Priya: i'll try to get legal's initial redlines by 6/16.
[05:44] Diego: will stand up staging by 6/12 if we get the spec.
[05:48] (end)

Notes: natural speech patterns with filler removed at times; occasional mis-transcribed product names (K-V cash) replicated to keep export authenticity. References: will attach pricing spreadsheet, pilot plan doc, SOC2 packet, SOW draft link in follow-up email.
